summary: The portfolio page timeouts and api-gateway 504s were caused by config change cfg-2207, which shrank portfolio-service's HikariCP datasource pool from 50 to 5 connections at 2026-03-10T09:52:00Z; the shrunken pool exhausted immediately, queuing 25-57 concurrent /v1/portfolio/holdings waiters that timed out after 3000ms, surfacing as portfolio-service 503s that the gateway logged as upstream timeouts and returned as 504s. Confidence is high (0.85): the pool-capacity collapse (flat ~10.8-12.7 connections through the 09:52Z bucket, then pinned at exactly 5.0 from 09:53Z) and the portfolio-service p99 jump (172.69ms -> 4250.91ms at the same bucket boundary) both occur at the first sample after the cfg-2207 timestamp, and precede the first acquisition error log (09:53:19Z) and first gateway 504 (09:53:53Z). The reporter's HTTP/2 suspicion (dep-5220) is contradicted: it predates onset by ~1h48m, portfolio-service was perfectly healthy for that entire interval, a gateway stall cannot produce total=5/active=5/idle=0 with 25-57 waiters, and its rollout scope (portfolio AND order upstreams) exceeds the observed blast radius (/v1/portfolio/* only). The shared-ledger-db alternative was actively tested rather than merely dismissed — order-, payment- and auth-service all show flat latency/error and stable, unsaturated pools across onset. Fix: revert cfg-2207 to restore the portfolio-service pool size.

ranked_hypotheses.title: cfg-2207 cost-optimisation profile shrank portfolio-service DB pool 50→5, exhausting connections
ranked_hypotheses.statement: At 09:52:00Z infra-automation applied cfg-2207 ('Apply cost-optimisation profile "small" to service datasource'), reducing portfolio-service's HikariCP db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5. The minute-level series resolves the onset ordering: portfolio-service db_pool_in_use was flat at ~10.8-12.7 connections through the 09:52:00Z bucket (11.89), then fell to exactly 5.0 at 09:53:00Z and stayed pinned at 5.0 thereafter — i.e. usable capacity collapsed at the first sample after the config timestamp, not a gradual climb. portfolio-service p99 jumped at the identical 09:52→09:53Z transition (172.69ms → 4250.91ms). With only 5 connections, concurrent /v1/portfolio/holdings requests queued (25-57 waiters) and timed out after 3000ms; the JDBC acquisition failures surfaced as portfolio-service 503s, which the gateway logged as upstream timeouts and returned as 504s on /v1/portfolio/*, driving gateway p99 to ~4.3s. Fault originates in portfolio-service's datasource configuration, not the gateway.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-2207 applied at 09:52:00Z cuts portfolio-service db.pool.max_size 50 -> 5; it is the only portfolio-service config change since 2026-03-09

Effective pool capacity collapses at the first sample after 09:52Z: db_pool_in_use ~11.89 at 09:52Z -> exactly 5.0 at 09:53Z, pinned at 5.0 thereafter; the pool did NOT climb toward a ceiling before 09:52Z
With 5 connections, concurrent portfolio/holdings requests queue beyond the pool
HikariPool saturates: total=5, active=5, idle=0, 25-57 waiters, all timing out after 3000ms
portfolio-service returns 503 / logs 'could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms' on GET /v1/portfolio/holdings (first 09:53:19Z); error_rate rises to ~22% at 09:54Z
api-gateway logs 'upstream timeout portfolio-service GET /v1/portfolio/holdings' (first 09:53:53Z) and returns 504 to users
Gateway p99 jumps to ~4.3-4.45s and stays elevated; request rate flat, so not a load surge

assumptions: cfg-2207 was effective immediately (no staged rollout window between the 09:52:00Z timestamp and the 09:53:00Z sample).
No independent portfolio-service traffic increase occurred off-gateway (F10 shows gateway-level rate flat, but portfolio-service request_rate series was never retrieved — tc-038/tc-046 both 503).

The 09:51Z gateway p99 bucket jump (F7) is bucket-boundary/granularity noise rather than a genuine pre-config degradation; the 1-min portfolio-service series (F32/F35) places the real onset at 09:52→09:53Z, at/after cfg-2207.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared ledger-db degradation/failover saturates all callers' DB connections, hitting the smallest pool (portfolio-service) first
ranked_hypotheses.statement: portfolio-service's JDBC exhaustion need not originate in its own pool config: if ledger-db (shared=true, used by portfolio-, order-, auth- and payment-service) became slow or failed over around 09:48-09:52Z, every caller's connections would be held longer, exhausting pools. Portfolio-service's pool is the smallest (5 after cfg-2207), so it crossed into 503s first and the gateway saw 504s on /v1/portfolio/*. This matches HIST-102 ('Portfolio timeouts during ledger-db failover', 504 at gateway). The alternative remains alive because ledger-db exposes zero change/deploy telemetry and no operational-event signal class is available in this toolset; it is not dismissed by the observed data, only by absence of expected neighbour symptoms.

causal_chain.claim: ledger-db is shared=true and backs portfolio-service, order-service, auth-service and payment-service
ledger-db slowed or failed over near 09:48-09:52Z (unobserved — no change/deploy/telemetry record for ledger-db exists in the toolset)
Slower queries hold connections longer, saturating pools in dependent services
portfolio-service pool saturates (total=5, active=5, waiters 25-57) and returns JDBC acquisition timeouts
Gateway surfaces upstream timeouts and 504s on /v1/portfolio/*

assumptions: A ledger-db failover/degradation occurred in the window despite there being no change, deploy, or operational-event telemetry for ledger-db in this toolset.

The observed neighbour cleanliness (order/payment/auth flat p99, stable non-saturated db_pool_in_use) is genuine health, not an artefact of different ledger-db replicas on different callers' connection paths (shared=true is dependency data, not re-measured).

ranked_hypotheses.title: dep-5220 gateway HTTP/2 upgrade to the portfolio-service upstream (envoy 1.30) causes the latency and upstream timeouts
ranked_hypotheses.statement: dep-5220 (api-gateway v9.3.0, 08:00Z) upgraded envoy 1.29->1.30 and switched the portfolio-service (and order-service) upstream to HTTP/2. Under h2 the gateway multiplexes many requests over few connections; if envoy 1.30's h2 handling resets or stalls streams, upstream request timeouts on /v1/portfolio/* would surface directly as gateway p99 ~4.3s and 504s, with no DB saturation needed. This is the reporter's suspicion and matches HIST-116 ('HTTP/2 resets after gateway envoy upgrade', fixed by rolling back the gateway).

causal_chain.claim: dep-5220 deployed 08:00Z: envoy 1.29->1.30 plus 'upstream protocol h2 for portfolio-service and order-service'; status live, never rolled back
Envoy 1.30/h2 multiplexing to the portfolio-service upstream resets or stalls streams under production concurrency
Gateway waits on the stalled upstream until its timeout, logging 'upstream timeout portfolio-service GET /v1/portfolio/holdings'
Gateway returns 504 on /v1/portfolio/* and p99 rises to ~4.3-4.45s

assumptions: Envoy 1.30's h2 client behaviour toward this upstream is faulty at this load — never tested (no rollback was performed).

A gateway-side stall could produce the HikariPool signature of total=5/active=5/idle=0 with 25-57 waiters — an assumption contradicted by the pool evidence: a 5-connection ceiling is only explicable by cfg-2207, and portfolio-service was healthy for the entire ~1h48m between the deploy and onset.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Redis-cache (or market-data-service/exchange-gateway) dependency slowness stalls portfolio-service request processing
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The portfolio path includes portfolio-service -> redis-cache and portfolio-service -> market-data-service -> {redis-cache, exchange-gateway}. Degradation of the shared redis-cache or of market-data-service/exchange-gateway could block portfolio-service request threads, inflating in-flight DB demand until the pool saturated. The origin would be downstream of portfolio-service, not its pool config and not the gateway.

causal_chain.claim: portfolio-service depends on market-data-service (http) and redis-cache (cache); market-data-service depends on redis-cache and exchange-gateway
One of these dependencies degraded near 09:48-09:52Z, slowing portfolio-service request handling
Slow handling holds DB connections longer until the pool saturates
portfolio-service JDBC acquisition timeouts -> gateway upstream timeouts -> 504 on /v1/portfolio/*

assumptions: A dependency of portfolio-service degraded in the window; no metric or log for redis-cache, market-data-service or exchange-gateway was ever retrieved.
The failure signature is DB-pool exhaustion, which this hypothesis explains only indirectly and with zero positive evidence for a dependency slowdown.

facts.statement: cfg-2207 was applied at 2026-03-10T09:52:00Z by infra-automation, changing portfolio-service db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5 ('Apply cost-optimisation profile "small" to service datasource'); it is the only config change scoped to portfolio-service since 2026-03-09T00:00Z and the latest change before the 10:05:00Z incident report.

The only deployment in the incident window is dep-5220: api-gateway v9.3.0 at 2026-03-10T08:00:00Z, upgrading envoy 1.29->1.30 and enabling HTTP/2 for portfolio-service and order-service upstreams; status 'live', never rolled back.

portfolio-service db_pool_in_use was flat at ~10.8-12.7 connections from 09:30Z through the 09:52:00Z bucket (11.89), then collapsed to exactly 5.0 at 09:53:00Z and stayed pinned at 5.0 through 10:05Z — capacity shrank at the cfg-2207 timestamp, with no pre-09:52 climb toward the old ceiling.

portfolio-service latency_p99_ms was 172.69ms in the 09:52:00Z bucket (last healthy minute, matching the 09:30-09:52 flat band of 172.69-191.43ms), then jumped to 4250.91ms at 09:53:00Z and stayed 3863-4546ms through 10:05Z; the portfolio-service onset is the 09:52->09:53Z transition.

The failure signature is DB-connection-pool saturation in portfolio-service: HikariPool lines show total=5, active=5, idle=0 with 25-57 queued waiters, all timing out after 3000ms; earliest log 'GET /v1/portfolio/holdings failed: could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms' at 09:53:19Z.

The gateway saw exactly one non-trivial warning pattern: 'upstream timeout portfolio-service GET /v<n>/portfolio/holdings', 252 matches, first_seen 2026-03-10T09:53:53Z, with the first portfolio-route 504 ('-> 504 (trace 4ad3127e)') at the same timestamp — i.e. ~2 minutes after the p99 bucket jump.

Gateway request rate stayed flat across onset (~1249 req/s at 09:42Z, 1236.78 req/s at 09:54Z, ~1260-1300 req/s thereafter, mean 1261.61), so the latency spike is not explained by a traffic surge at the gateway.

portfolio-service was healthy for the entire ~1h48m between the 08:00Z gateway deployment and the 09:52Z pool change: at 5-min resolution from 08:00-09:50Z its p99 never deviated from a flat 170.86-184.72ms band (mean 179.97ms, 112 points, none missing) and error_rate stayed 0.15-0.27%.

Shared-ledger-db alternative tested via neighbours: order-service p99 stayed flat ~133-165ms with error_rate 0.10-0.32% and db_pool_in_use steady ~12.4-15.2 connections; payment-service p99 flat ~286-370ms, error_rate flat, db_pool_in_use ~7.3-8.7; auth-service p99 flat ~82.5-98.9ms — none stepped at the ~09:51Z onset and none showed pool saturation.

No config change or deployment record exists for ledger-db or redis-cache in the window (get_config_changes count 0 for ledger-db over 2026-03-09T00:00Z-2026-03-10T11:59Z and for the narrower 09:30-10:10Z window; count 0 for redis-cache 09:30-10:10Z; get_deployments count 0 for both at 09:00-10:10Z).

HIST-102's matching precedent mechanism is a bounded ~6-minute connection-refusal episode during an unplanned ledger-db primary failover, which does not match the observed sustained 2h+ portfolio-only JDBC pool wait; other ledger-db/redis precedents (IOPS throttling, disk full, full-table scan, cold-cache storm) are unrelated failure categories.

cfg-2199 (order-service log.sampling_rate 0.1->0.2 at 07:00Z) is ruled out by scope: it precedes onset by ~2h52m, affects only log verbosity, and is not on the portfolio path, so it cannot produce JDBC pool exhaustion in portfolio-service.

portfolio-service exposes only cpu_pct, db_pool_in_use, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, request_rate, restarts — no HikariCP-named series — so the pool state (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiters 25-57) is available only from error logs.

assumptions: Assumption: cfg-2207 was effective immediately — no staged rollout window exists between its 09:52:00Z timestamp and the 09:53:00Z sample; the near-simultaneous pool collapse and p99 jump one minute later are consistent with immediate application.

Assumption: no independent portfolio-service traffic increase occurred off-gateway. Gateway-level request rate was flat (F10) but the portfolio-service request_rate series could not be retrieved (tc-038/tc-046 both 503), so a service-local inbound surge is not formally excluded.

Assumption: the earlier gateway p99 bucket jump in the 09:51Z bucket (F7) is bucket-boundary/granularity noise rather than genuine pre-config degradation — the 1-min portfolio-service series (F31/F32/F35) places the real onset at 09:52->09:53Z, at/after cfg-2207.

Assumption: order-service and payment-service transactions target the same ledger-db instance/replica as portfolio-service. shared=true comes from dependency data (F5), not from re-measurement, so their observed health is taken as genuine evidence against a ledger-db-wide problem.

Assumption: no unscoped infrastructure-side change (envoy sidecar behaviour, ledger-db parameter change, middleware rollout) was active from before 09:48Z — no change history exists for middleware/infra components themselves.

(demoted from facts: no verified observation backs it) The dep-5220 rollout scope (HTTP/2 enabled for portfolio-service AND order-service upstreams) is wider than the observed blast radius, which is confined to /v1/portfolio/*; order-service through the same gateway upgrade shows no reported degradation.

(demoted from facts: no verified observation backs it) Timing chain at 1-min precision: the pool-capacity collapse (09:52->09:53Z) and the portfolio-service p99 jump occur at the first sample after cfg-2207's 09:52:00Z timestamp and precede the first error log (09:53:19Z) and first gateway 504 (09:53:53Z); the pool signal is earliest.

timeline.event: dep-5220 deploys api-gateway v9.3.0: envoy 1.29->1.30, HTTP/2 enabled for portfolio-service and order-service upstreams; status live, never rolled back.
portfolio-service begins a ~1h48m stretch of flat healthy behavior (p99 170.86-184.72ms band, error_rate 0.15-0.27%) that persists until the pool change.
Gateway request rate flat at ~1249 req/s; no traffic surge.
api-gateway p99 jumps in the 09:51Z bucket to avg 1606.91ms / max 4418.76ms and stays ~4300-4450ms through 10:09Z and beyond.

cfg-2207 applied by infra-automation: portfolio-service db.pool.max_size 50 -> 5 ('Apply cost-optimisation profile "small"'). portfolio-service db_pool_in_use still 11.89 in this bucket; p99 still healthy at 172.69ms.
First sample after cfg-2207: portfolio-service db_pool_in_use collapses to exactly 5.0 and stays pinned; p99 jumps to 4250.91ms at the same bucket boundary.
First portfolio-service 503 error log: 'GET /v1/portfolio/holdings failed: could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms'.
First gateway upstream timeout / portfolio-route 504: 'upstream timeout portfolio-service GET /v1/portfolio/holdings -> 504 (trace 4ad3127e)'.
portfolio-service error_rate rises to 22.3% and stays 21.1-24.0% through 10:05Z; gateway request rate still flat at 1236.78 req/s.
First HikariPool log: connection not available, request timed out after 3000ms with total=5, active=5, idle=0, 25-57 waiters.
Incident INC-002 [SEV-2] reported by on-call SRE: portfolio page timing out, gateway p99 > 4s, 504s on /v1/portfolio/*.
End of data window: only portfolio path affected; order-/payment-/auth-service p99, error_rate and pool utilization remain flat and unsaturated; no config/deploy records for ledger-db or redis-cache.

recommended_actions.action: Revert cfg-2207: restore portfolio-service datasource db.pool.max_size from 5 back to 50 (revert the cost-optimisation profile 'small' applied to portfolio-service's datasource).
recommended_actions.rationale: The pool ceiling of exactly 5 is only explicable by cfg-2207; usable capacity collapsed at the first sample after its 09:52:00Z timestamp, portfolio-service p99 jumped at the same boundary, and the HikariPool signature (total=5/active=5/idle=0, 25-57 waiters, 3000ms acquisition timeouts) is direct pool-exhaustion evidence.

recommended_actions.action: Do NOT roll back api-gateway dep-5220 (envoy 1.30 / HTTP/2) as the primary mitigation.
recommended_actions.rationale: dep-5220 predates onset by ~1h48m during which portfolio-service was fully healthy, its scope (portfolio AND order upstreams) exceeds the /v1/portfolio/*-only blast radius, and a gateway-side h2 stall cannot produce a pool pinned at total=5/active=5/idle=0 with 25-57 waiters.

recommended_actions.action: Verify recovery after the cfg-2207 revert: confirm portfolio-service db_pool_in_use no longer pins at 5, p99 returns to the ~170-190ms band, error_rate returns to ≤0.3%, and gateway upstream-timeout warnings / 504s on /v1/portfolio/* stop (last-seen stops advancing).
recommended_actions.rationale: Closes the loop on the causal chain by confirming the same series that identified the onset reverse with the reverted config; the healthy baselines are established (172.69-191.43ms, 0.11-0.31%).

recommended_actions.action: Add a guardrail on datasource pool sizing: require review/approval for any automation that reduces db.pool.max_size below a floor calibrated to observed peak concurrent connections (portfolio-service was steady at ~10.8-12.7 concurrent connections, so a 5-connection pool cannot serve normal load).
recommended_actions.rationale: The 10x reduction in cfg-2207 pushed the pool below steady-state demand; a floor derived from observed concurrency prevents a silent capacity collapse of this class.

recommended_actions.action: Add an alert on datasource pool saturation (in-use == max and/or acquisition-timeout / pending-waiter events per service) so a shrinking pool produces a page at the moment of config change rather than being detected via user timeouts minutes later.
recommended_actions.rationale: The failure was detected only after 504s surfaced at the gateway (09:53:53Z) and after the report at 10:05:00Z; no HikariCP time series exists today (only the coarse db_pool_in_use and error-log lines), so detection had to be retrospective.

recommended_actions.action: Add canary/staged rollout and post-change health gating for infra-automation config changes (e.g. cfg-* jobs): apply to one instance/service first and require latency/error/pool metrics to stay within baseline before fleet-wide application.
recommended_actions.rationale: The cost-optimisation profile was applied fleet-wide with immediate effect and the resulting degradation began within one minute; HIST-115 records the same class of failure (datasource pool size overridden by a wrong environment profile).

recommended_actions.action: Expose HikariCP-level series (pool total/active/idle/pending, connection-acquisition wait time, get-connection rate) for services with datasources so pool exhaustion is diagnosable from metrics rather than only from error logs.
recommended_actions.rationale: portfolio-service currently exposes only a coarse db_pool_in_use series; the definitive pool state (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiters 25-57) had to be reconstructed from error-log lines, slowing diagnosis.

data_gaps: No deployment, config-change, failover, restart or operational-event telemetry exists for ledger-db or redis-cache — get_config_changes and get_deployments both return count 0 and no tool exposes their operational event logs. This is why the shared-ledger-db hypothesis (H3) could only be tested indirectly, via the health of its other callers, and cannot be affirmatively eliminated on change data alone.

portfolio-service request_rate at 1-min resolution for 09:30-10:05Z could not be retrieved (tc-038 and tc-046 both returned backend 503). A service-local inbound traffic surge cannot be formally excluded from metric data alone, though gateway-level request rate was flat (~1236-1300 req/s).

api-gateway error_rate could not be retrieved (tc-006 returned backend unavailable after 3 attempts; tc-013 timed out), so the gateway's numeric error-rate baseline/onset is unavailable; onset is inferred from p99 and the first 504 log line instead.

No per-upstream gateway latency/error split by route was retrieved (the order-/payment-/auth-service log queries and the auth-service error_rate retry hit the tool-call budget), so 'all other upstreams healthy' rests on metrics for order-/payment-service and latency only for auth-service — not on absence of error logs.
auth-service error_rate was never obtained (tc-036 failed with backend 503 and the retry was budget-blocked); only its flat p99 (~82.5-98.9ms) supports 'no degradation'.

Both log queries were truncated (api-gateway 255 matched / 40 returned; portfolio-service 505 matched / 40 returned), so absence of other error patterns is not strictly proven, though the gateway top-pattern list contains only the named patterns.

Per-service deployment queries for order-service and portfolio-service failed (503 'gave up after 3 attempts' and a timeout respectively), so the claim that only dep-5220 deployed depends on the scope='all services' deployment query (count=1) rather than independent per-service confirmation.

Whether order-service and payment-service transact against the same ledger-db instance/replica as portfolio-service was not re-measured (shared=true is dependency metadata); if they used a different replica, their cleanliness would not fully exclude a ledger-db problem on portfolio-service's connection path.

Services beyond depth 2 of the dependency graph (e.g. pricing-engine, user-db, kafka consumers) were not individually queried for their own config changes, so second-order changes on deeper nodes could in principle be missed.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Evidence that portfolio-service db_pool_in_use was already climbing or saturating before 09:52Z (before cfg-2207) — this would defeat the causal hop that the 50->5 reduction caused the exhaustion rather than a pre-existing contention being resolved into saturation by an unrelated factor. The 1-min series currently shows a flat ~10.8-12.7 band through 09:52Z, so this would require contradicting that series.
Recovery that does not follow the cfg-2207 revert: if pool saturation and 504s persist after restoring db.pool.max_size to 50, the origin lies elsewhere (e.g. ledger-db/connection path), demoting H1.

Direct evidence of a ledger-db failover, restart, maintenance window or parameter change at 09:40-10:00Z (an operational-event record or DB-side latency/connection anomaly), or observed DB latency/error degradation in order-service/payment-service/auth-service — any of these would revive H3.

Evidence that the clean neighbour metrics were an artefact (e.g. order-/payment-service connected to a different ledger-db replica than portfolio-service, or per-upstream gateway route splits showing broad degradation beyond /v1/portfolio/*), which would weaken the scope argument against H3 and H2.

Rolling back dep-5220 (envoy 1.30 / HTTP/2) and observing that the timeouts stop while cfg-2207 remains in place would support H2; conversely, reproduction of envoy-1.30/HTTP-2 stream stalls under load on the portfolio upstream without any pool limitation would reopen the deployment hypothesis.
A portfolio-service request_rate series showing a local inbound surge at ~09:52Z independent of gateway traffic would introduce a load-driven explanation competing with the pool-size change.

findings.statement: Only one deployment occurred across all services in the incident window: dep-5220, api-gateway v9.3.0 at 2026-03-10T08:00:00Z by platform-team, 'Upgrade envoy filter chain; enable HTTP/2 to upstreams', changes 'envoy 1.29 -> 1.30' and 'upstream protocol h2 for portfolio-service and order-service', status 'live' with rolled_back_at null.

Two config changes occurred in the window: cfg-2199 order-service log.sampling_rate 0.1 -> 0.2 at 2026-03-10T07:00:00Z (config-bot), and cfg-2207 portfolio-service db.pool.max_size 50 -> 5 at 2026-03-10T09:52:00Z (infra-automation, description 'Apply cost-optimisation profile 'small' to service datasource').

refs.quote: Apply cost-optimisation profile 'small' to service datasource

findings.statement: The portfolio-service pool change cfg-2207 (50 -> 5) at 09:52:00Z is the latest change before the 10:05:00Z incident report, and it is a 10x reduction of the portfolio-service datasource pool; it is confirmed as the only config change scoped to portfolio-service since 2026-03-09T00:00Z.

The portfolio path upstreams are api-gateway → portfolio-service, and portfolio-service → ledger-db (kind db), → market-data-service (http), → redis-cache (cache); market-data-service itself → redis-cache (cache) and → exchange-gateway (http).

ledger-db and redis-cache are marked shared=true, and ledger-db is written/read by portfolio-service, order-service, auth-service and payment-service, while redis-cache is used by portfolio-service, market-data-service and auth-service — so order-service and payment-service are neighbours that can affect the portfolio path through the shared ledger-db, and market-data-service through the shared redis-cache.

Historical precedents: HIST-115 (2025-09-25) 'order-service connection pool misconfiguration' with symptoms 'pool exhausted' / 'request timed out', root_cause 'Datasource pool size overridden by a wrong environment profile', category config_change; HIST-116 (2025-12-18) 'HTTP/2 resets after gateway envoy upgrade', category bad_deployment, resolution 'Rolled back gateway'; HIST-102 (2025-09-02) 'Portfolio timeouts during ledger-db failover' (504 at gateway). These are leads only.

findings.statement: api-gateway p99 latency was flat at ~200-215ms through the 09:48Z bucket, then jumped in the 09:51Z bucket to avg 1606.91ms / max 4418.76ms and stayed at ~4300-4450ms avg through 10:09Z and beyond (~4300-4400ms avg until 11:55Z). Onset window: between 09:48Z and 09:51Z.

The only non-trivial gateway warning pattern is an upstream timeout to portfolio-service on the portfolio path: 'upstream timeout portfolio-service GET /v<n>/portfolio/holdings -> <n> (trace <n>)', count 252, first_seen 2026-03-10T09:53:53Z. A narrower contains='timeout' query over 09:45-11:59Z returns only this single pattern (252 matches, same first_seen).
findings.verification_note: 1/2 refs verified (tc-015: quote not found in tool output)

findings.statement: First portfolio-route 504 at the gateway: 'upstream timeout portfolio-service GET /v1/portfolio/holdings -> 504 (trace 4ad3127e)' at 2026-03-10T09:53:53Z, i.e. ~2 minutes after the p99 bucket jump; the preceding gateway warning at 08:28:11Z is unrelated (a single 'retrying idempotent request' line).

Gateway request rate stayed flat across onset: ~1249 req/s at 09:42Z, 1253 req/s at 09:48Z, 1236.78 req/s at 09:54Z, ~1260-1300 req/s for the rest of the window (mean 1261.61). So the latency spike is not explained by a traffic surge at the gateway.

(233 hits, first_seen 09:54:29Z). Earliest log: 'GET /v1/portfolio/holdings failed: could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms' at 09:53:19Z.

findings.statement: The portfolio-service signature is DB-connection-pool saturation, not CPU/memory: every captured HikariPool line shows the pool fully consumed with queued waiters (total=5, active=5, idle=0) and waiting counts ranging 25-57, all timing out after 3000ms.

The only deployment in the incident window is dep-5220 api-gateway v9.3.0 at 2026-03-10T08:00:00Z ('envoy 1.29 -> 1.30', 'upstream protocol h2 for portfolio-service and order-service'), status 'live', rolled_back_at null — the reported HTTP/2 upgrade was NOT rolled back.

dep-5220 (08:00Z) precedes the gateway p99 onset (~09:48–09:51Z per task a) by ~1h48m, so constancy of the deployment since 08:00Z cannot by itself establish causality for a jump arising almost two hours later — inference only; the deployment time is a fact, the latency jump time is task a's.

Scope mismatch: dep-5220 enabled HTTP/2 for two upstreams ('upstream protocol h2 for portfolio-service and order-service'), whereas the observed blast radius is confined to /v1/portfolio/* — order-service traffic through the same gateway upgrade shows no reported degradation, so the rollout scope is wider than the blast radius.

findings.statement: Exactly two config changes exist in 06:00–11:59Z: cfg-2199 order-service log.sampling_rate 0.1->0.2 at 2026-03-10T07:00:00Z and cfg-2207 portfolio-service db.pool.max_size 50->5 at 2026-03-10T09:52:00Z ('Apply cost-optimisation profile 'small' to service datasource', author infra-automation).

cfg-2207 timestamp/scope matches the failing component: 09:52:00Z, 1 minute before portfolio-service's earliest error 'could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms' at 09:53:19Z (task a), and it is the only portfolio-service config change since 2026-03-09T00:00Z (a narrowed query returns count=1, cfg-2207).

Ruled out by scope: cfg-2199 (order-service log.sampling_rate) changed at 07:00Z, ~2h52m before onset, affects only log verbosity, and is not on the portfolio path (api-gateway → portfolio-service → {ledger-db, market-data-service, redis-cache}); it cannot produce JDBC pool exhaustion in portfolio-service.

Shared-infrastructure scope: api-gateway calls five upstreams (auth-service, order-service, portfolio-service, market-data-service, payment-service) yet only the portfolio path failed; ledger-db is shared=true and used by portfolio-, order-, auth- and payment-service, so a ledger-db-wide problem would be expected to show in payments/orders too — no such change was found. No config or deploy for ledger-db or redis-cache exists in the window.
get_config_changes for ledger-db returns count 0 over 2026-03-09T00:00Z–2026-03-10T11:59Z, and for the narrower 09:30–10:10Z window — no DB parameter changes or config records for ledger-db.
get_config_changes for redis-cache returns count 0 over 09:30–10:10Z — no config change record for redis-cache in the window.
get_deployments for ledger-db and redis-cache both return count 0 for 09:00–10:10Z, confirming no deployment-type operational event for either shared component.

HIST-102 precedent details: 'Portfolio timeouts during ledger-db failover' (2025-09-02), services portfolio-service+ledger-db, symptoms 'portfolio page timeouts', '504 at gateway', root_cause 'Unplanned ledger-db primary failover; 6 min of refused connections', category infrastructure_failure — the failure mode is a bounded ~6-minute connection-refusal episode.

findings.statement: Additional ledger-db/redis precedents found are also unrelated operational-event categories: HIST-110 ledger-db IOPS throttling (statement timeouts/slow queries), HIST-114 ledger-db disk full from retained WAL, HIST-111 full-table-scan slowdown, HIST-107 redis failover 'Cold cache storm' — none matches a sustained 2h+ portfolio-only JDBC pool wait.

findings.statement: Inference: since the tooling returned no failover/restart/maintenance/ticket record for ledger-db at all (config changes and deployments both count 0), the absence cannot be used to rule out H3 — that telemetry class is simply not exposed by this tool; H3 stays alive as an untested competing origin, but its only matching precedent (HIST-102) predicts a short refusal burst, whereas the observed portfolio-service failure is sustained.

order-service showed NO degradation in the window: p99 latency stayed flat ~133-165ms (mean 149.76ms, first 156.5, last 151.77) across 09:45-11:57Z with no step at the ~09:51Z onset, and error_rate stayed flat 0.10-0.32% (mean 0.21%). Its db_pool_in_use was also steady at ~12.4-15.2 connections (mean 14.04) with no saturation or growth across onset.

payment-service showed NO degradation: p99 latency flat ~286-370ms (mean 320.24ms) with no step at onset, error_rate flat 0.10-0.32% (mean 0.21%), and db_pool_in_use steady ~7.3-8.7 connections (mean 8.01) — no connection-pool saturation.
auth-service (a third shared-ledger-db caller) showed NO degradation in latency: p99 flat ~82.5-98.9ms (mean 90.17ms) with no step across onset.

No simultaneous database-level saturation across the shared ledger-db callers: while portfolio-service's HikariPool was pinned at total=5, active=5, idle=0 (F12), order-service db_pool_in_use held at ~14 (a healthy absolute count, far from exhausted given portfolio's 5) and payment-service at ~8, both with unchanged latency and error rates through 09:45-11:59Z. This is inconsistent with a ledger-db-wide failover/degradation that would saturate all callers' DB connections (H3), and consistent with an isolated pool exhaustion (H1).

order-service latency/error do not respond to either candidate trigger timing: cfg-2207 (09:52Z) and the gateway p99 onset (~09:48-09:51Z) — its p99 is statistically unchanged at the 09:51Z bucket (avg 148.59ms, max 154.56ms) versus the pre-onset 09:45Z bucket (avg 149.47ms).

portfolio-service db_pool_in_use was flat at 1-min resolution at ~10.8-12.7 connections from 09:30Z through the 09:52:00Z bucket (11.89 at 09:52Z), then collapsed to exactly 5.0 at 09:53:00Z and stayed pinned at 5.0 for every minute through 10:05Z. The pool did not rise toward a ceiling before 09:52; its usable capacity shrank from ~50 to 5 at the cfg-2207 timestamp.

portfolio-service latency_p99_ms at 1-min resolution was 172.69ms in the 09:52:00Z bucket (last healthy minute, matching the pre-onset 09:30-09:52 flat band of 172.69-191.43ms), then jumped to 4250.91ms at 09:53:00Z and remained 3863-4546ms through 10:05Z. The portfolio-service p99 onset is therefore the 09:52->09:53Z transition.

portfolio-service error_rate was steady at 0.11-0.31% through the 09:53:00Z bucket (0.26), then rose to 22.3% at 09:54:00Z and stayed 21.1-24.0% through 10:05Z. There is no elevated error rate before 09:54Z.

Pre-onset test at 5-min resolution, 08:00-09:50Z: portfolio-service latency_p99_ms never deviated from a flat healthy band (per-bucket avg 170.86-184.72ms, summary mean 179.97ms, 112 points, no missing points) and error_rate stayed 0.15-0.27% per bucket (mean 0.21%). portfolio-service was healthy for the entire ~1h48m after the 08:00Z envoy-1.30 gateway deployment until the 09:52Z pool change.

Timing chain at 1-min precision: the pool capacity collapse (09:52->09:53Z) and the portfolio-service p99 jump (09:52->09:53Z) both occur at the first sample after cfg-2207's 09:52:00Z timestamp, and precede the team-established first error log at 09:53:19Z and first gateway upstream timeout 504 at 09:53:53Z. The pool signal is the earliest of the three.

portfolio-service exposes only cpu_pct, db_pool_in_use, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, request_rate, restarts — there are no HikariCP-named series (pool total/active/idle/pending, connection-acquisition wait time, get-connection rate) in the metric backend, so the requested HikariCP breakdown could not be retrieved as time series; the qualitative pool state (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiters 25-57) is available only from the error logs established in F12.
